source_metadata.title: Comparison of Treatment Result Between Anticoagulation Alone and Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis Plus Anticoagulation in Acute Lower Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis
source_metadata.source_type: Original Article; retrospective single-center registry analysis

source_content_warnings.detail: The Results narrative states there was no significant difference in comorbid conditions, but Table 1 reports malignancy in 7.5% of ACA vs 24.1% of CDT patients with P=0.017. Table 1 is preserved as reported and the contradiction is flagged rather than reconciled.
The Results narrative reports P=0.894 for mean age, whereas Table 1 reports P=0.953. The age atom follows Table 1 and preserves this discrepancy here.
The abstract reports CDT overall thrombus removal as 87.0%, whereas Results reports 87.1% (74/85). The atom uses the explicit fraction and Results value 87.1%.

source_content_warnings.location: Results prose page 31 vs Table 3 page 30
source_content_warnings.detail: The prose reverses the calf-vein group order in one sentence; Table 3 clearly reports ACA 36/38 (94.7%) and CDT 9/9 (100.0%). The atom follows Table 3.

extraction_limitations: Primary-study assertions were extracted; background claims attributed to cited literature were not reclassified as findings generated by this study.
The source does not report a funding statement or data-availability statement; these were not invented as atoms.

The source reports four transfusion-requiring puncture-site bleeds after CDT while also stating there was no major bleeding, but it does not provide an operational major-bleeding definition; the extraction preserves both reports without reconciling them.
No adjusted effect estimates or confidence intervals for the principal between-group comparisons are reported in the source.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study objective was to compare clinical outcomes of anticoagulation alone with catheter-directed thrombolysis plus anticoagulation in patients with acute lower-extremity DVT.
The investigators performed a retrospective analysis of a single-center registry and reviewed 149 patients with DVT treated from January 2011 through December 2015.

population.label: Adults with acute lower-extremity DVT included in the single-center retrospective registry

atoms.canonical_statement: Inclusion criteria were age greater than 20 years, acute DVT with a first episode of swelling symptoms, symptom duration under 14 days, and life expectancy greater than 2 years.

population.label: Study inclusion population
inclusion_criteria: Acute DVT with a first episode of swelling symptoms

atoms.canonical_statement: Exclusion criteria included uncontrolled hypertension, stroke within the prior 3 months, pregnancy or another concomitant chronic or potentially life-threatening disease, bleeding disorders, recent surgery, and gastrointestinal or other major bleeding within the prior 3 weeks.

population.label: Study exclusion criteria
exclusion_criteria: Pregnancy or other concomitant chronic or potentially life-threatening disease
Gastrointestinal or other major bleeding event in the last 3 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were divided into a CDT group that received catheter-directed thrombolysis followed by anticoagulation and an ACA group that received anticoagulation alone.

atoms.canonical_statement: Thrombus removal was evaluated with follow-up CT venography, which was performed within at least the initial 6 months and when venous patency was clinically questioned.

atoms.canonical_statement: The anticoagulation-alone regimen used intravenous unfractionated heparin loading and continuous infusion to target an aPTT 1.5-2.5 times control, followed by warfarin targeting INR 2.0-3.0; warfarin was continued for at least 6 months.

concept.text: Anticoagulation alone: intravenous unfractionated heparin followed by warfarin

exposures.details: UFH loading and continuous infusion with therapeutic aPTT 1.5-2.5 times control; conversion to warfarin with INR target 2.0-3.0; warfarin for at least 6 months.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study administered CDT to patients with proximal lower-extremity DVT, symptoms for 14 days or less, good functional status, life expectancy of at least 2 years, and low bleeding risk.

exposures.details: Selected for proximal lower-extremity DVT, symptoms <=14 days, good functional status, life expectancy >=2 years, low bleeding risk.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the CDT protocol, enoxaparin was started on the day of DVT diagnosis at 1.0 mg/kg.

exposures.details: Started on the day of DVT diagnosis in the CDT subsection.

atoms.canonical_statement: CDT access was obtained by ultrasound-guided puncture of the distal popliteal vein in the prone position, followed by placement of an 8-Fr introducer sheath, guidewire traversal of the thrombus, and positioning of a multisidehole infusion catheter within the thrombotic segment.
Urokinase was infused at 600-1,200 U/kg/h for 24-48 hours during CDT.

exposures.details: Reported dose range was 600-1,200 U/kg/h by continuous infusion.

atoms.canonical_statement: Heparin was infused through the access sheath during CDT to avoid thrombus formation; aPTT was measured every 4 hours and maintained at 1.5-2.0 times control.

exposures.details: aPTT measured every 4 hours and maintained at 1.5-2.0 times control.

atoms.canonical_statement: Venography was performed after 24-48 hours of CDT to monitor thrombolysis.

Categorical variables were compared with chi-square or Fisher exact tests, continuous variables with an independent-samples t-test, and long-term outcomes with a log-rank test; P<0.05 was considered significant.
The analyzed cohort comprised 120 patients in the anticoagulation-alone group and 29 patients in the CDT plus anticoagulation group.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that thrombus removal by lesion and recurrence-free rates showed no significant difference between the ACA and CDT groups.
The authors concluded that anticoagulation alone still has a crucial role in the treatment of DVT.
The authors identified the retrospective design and unavoidable selection bias as study limitations.
The authors identified the small CDT group relative to the ACA group as a study limitation.
The study could not evaluate post-thrombotic syndrome because the database did not support that assessment.
The authors stated that they had nothing to disclose.
